extracted.intended_audience: USPTO examining corps personnel and patent applicants/agents
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive standards governing Notice of Allowance, payment of issue/publication fees, deferral and simultaneous issuance requests, withdrawal from issue, post-allowance practice, and the USPTO quality-review process at the allowance/issue stage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent term extension/adjustment notice wording and eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Page three of the Notice of Allowance must state the patent term extension or adjustment in days and indicate the relevant extension/adjustment; if a continued prosecution application (CPA) was filed, the filing date of the most recent CPA determines the patent term extension/adjustment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Utility and plant applications filed on or after June 8, 1995 and before May 29, 2000 may be eligible for patent term extension (see 35 U.S.C. 154(b) and 37 CFR 1.701). Applications filed on or after May 29, 2000 may be eligible for patent term adjustment (see 35 U.S.C. 154(b) and 37 CFR 1.702-1.705, esp. 1.705(a)). The Notice language differs by filing date; applicants should consult USPTO website for more info.

rubrics_metrics.name: Issue fee timing and amount requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The issue fee (and any required publication fee) is due 3 months from the date of the Notice of Allowance; the Notice shows amounts which reflect any previously paid issue fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amount due is determined by the fees in effect under 37 CFR 1.18 as of date of submission of payment, so the amount paid may differ from the Notice. Applicants should verify current fee amounts at time of payment to avoid abandonment or lapsing (37 CFR 1.317). Small entity reduction (50%) applies to amounts due under 35 U.S.C. 41(a)(i) (issue fee).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Fee(s) Transmittal (PTOL-85B) and fee payment methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants and their attorneys/agents are urged to use the Fee(s) Transmittal form (PTOL-85B) when submitting payment of issue and publication fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Payments may be made by deposit account or credit card (form PTO 2038) but any such payment must specifically authorize charging for the “issue fee” or “fees due under 37 CFR 1.18.” Where deposit account info is added to PTOL-85B but the checkbox isn't checked, the deposit account will still be charged. If incorrect fee is supplied but applicant clearly intends to pay, a general or specific prior authorization may be treated as payment (37 CFR 1.311(b)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Routing and handling of post-allowance correspondence
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless otherwise directed, all post-allowance correspondence should be addressed to “Mail Stop Issue Fee” and Technology Center personnel should forward post-allowance correspondence to the Office of Initial Patent Examination (OIPE).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OIPE will scan and match papers to the application and forward to the appropriate Technology Center for processing. Duplicate filing of papers is discouraged and may be treated as failure to engage in reasonable efforts to conclude prosecution (37 CFR 1.704(c)(10)); do not both mail and fax the same correspondence unless specifically required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Director has no authority to extend issue fee payment time
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director has no authority to extend the time for paying the issue fee; intentional failure to pay within the 3 months is not unavoidable or unintentional delay.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must timely submit payment or use statutory remedies; petitions to extend this time are not permitted under the Director's authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deferring issuance of a patent (petition under 37 CFR 1.314)
rubrics_metrics.description: To request deferral of issuance, applicant must file a petition under 37 CFR 1.314 including the fee in § 1.17(h) and a showing of good and sufficient reasons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There is a public policy favoring issuance in regular course; absent extraordinary circumstances or regulatory requirements, deferral is granted for up to one month only. Typical situations like license negotiation, foreign filing time, collecting data for a continuation-in-part, or desire for simultaneous issuance are not extraordinary. Petition should be attached to PTOL-85B and clearly labeled 'Petition to Defer Issue; Attention: Office of Petitions.' A petition to defer is not appropriate until the issue fee is paid. Issuance cannot be deferred after patent number and issue date assigned unless application withdrawn from issue under 37 CFR 1.313.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simultaneous issuance request requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for simultaneous issuance will be granted only where a Notice of Allowance and Fee(s) Due (PTOL-85) has been mailed in each application to be issued simultaneously.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unless all applications have reached that stage or a specific regulation requires otherwise, simultaneous issuance generally will not be granted. The request must be submitted to Mail Stop Issue Fee, Commissioner for Patents, Attention: Office of Patent Publication, and must include for each application: (A) application number, (B) filing date, (C) inventor name(s), (D) title of invention, and (E) date of allowance. Separate PTOL-85B fee transmittals must accompany each application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted post-Notice filings and advice on timing
rubrics_metrics.description: After the Notice of Allowance has been mailed, only limited papers are appropriate (e.g., 'Query Printer Waiting', amendments under 37 CFR 1.312, information disclosure statements, and petitions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Corrected filing receipts typically will not be mailed after the Notice unless special circumstances exist. Applicants are advised to file any continuing applications, amendments, assignments, petitions, IDS, or other papers prior to paying the issue fee, preferably within one month after the Notice of Allowance, because the Office cannot ensure receipt/processing before patent issue date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal from issue statute and petition requirements (37 CFR 1.313)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications may be withdrawn from issue at initiative of the Office or upon petition by applicant under 37 CFR 1.313; to request withdrawal applicant must file a petition including the fee in § 1.17(h) and a showing of good and sufficient reasons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A petition is not required if a request for continued examination (RCE) under 37 CFR 1.114 is filed prior to payment of the issue fee. Petitions under 1.313(a) should be directed to the TC Director; petitions under 1.313(c) (after payment) should be directed to the Office of Petitions. Unless written communication that withdrawal has been effected is received, the issue fee must be timely submitted to avoid abandonment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for Office-initiated withdrawal after payment (37 CFR 1.313(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Once the issue fee has been paid, the Office will not withdraw the application from issue on its own initiative except for: (1) a mistake on the part of the Office; (2) a violation of § 1.56 or illegality in the application; (3) unpatentability of one or more claims; or (4) for interference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 35 U.S.C. 151 and 37 CFR 1.313(b) limit Office authority. Examples of reasons that do NOT warrant withdrawal after payment include permitting the examiner to consider an IDS, permitting the examiner to consider whether claims are unpatentable (unless it results in a determination of unpatentability), or to permit filing of a continuing application. Any notice withdrawing after payment must specify which 1.313(b)(1)-(4) condition exists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant-initiated withdrawal permitted reasons after payment (37 CFR 1.313(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: After payment of the issue fee, withdrawal upon applicant petition is allowed only for specified reasons in 37 CFR 1.313(c), including (A) unpatentability of one or more claims (petition accompanied by unequivocal statement and amendment(s) showing patentability), (B) consideration of a request for continued examination in compliance with § 1.114, or (C) express abandonment of the application (including in favor of a continuing application).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A petition under 1.313(c) must be clearly marked 'Petition under 37 CFR 1.313(c).' For utility or plant applications filed before June 8, 1995 and design applications, RCE practice may not apply. Filing methods: mail to Mail Stop Petitions, fax to Central Facsimile Number, or hand-carry to Office of Petitions. Hand-carrying is strongly advised to allow processing time; a grantable petition should ideally be received and granted at least three weeks prior to issue date to avoid publication/dissemination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing and effectiveness of withdrawal petitions
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition under 37 CFR 1.313 will not be effective to withdraw the application from issue unless it is actually received and granted by the appropriate officials before the date of issue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Withdrawal after payment may not avoid publication of application information if decided too late. The Office cannot ensure that a petition will be acted on prior to patent grant; applicants are cautioned to file RCEs or petitions in sufficient time before issue fee payment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure for withdrawal from issue before payment
rubrics_metrics.description: If the issue fee has not been paid and the payment deadline has not expired, the TC Director should prepare and mail a 'Withdrawal from Issue' letter (form ¶10.01), change application status to code 066, enter the letter in the file, place an Issue Information Label (Form 2016), and forward the application to the examiner for prompt action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For IFW applications, do not place the sticker; instead prepare a new Issue Classification sheet if subsequently allowed. The form letter must be signed by the TC Director. If issue and publication fees were submitted, applicant may request refund or credit; applicant may wait until application is again found allowable or held abandoned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure for withdrawal from issue after payment
rubrics_metrics.description: If the issue fee has been paid, prepare and mail a 'Notice of Withdrawal From Issue under 37 CFR 1.313(b)' (use form WDR-TCB1/TB2/TB3/TB4), and if a patent number and issue date were assigned, prepare a 'Withdrawal from Issue of' memorandum, e-mail it to Director of Office of Patent Publication, remove patent number from file wrapper, change status to code 066, and forward to examiner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The notice letter must be signed, date-stamped, and mailed no later than the Monday before the issue date to be effective to withdraw. Attach the notice and any memorandum to the application file. If prosecution reopens and issue fee was paid, applicant may request refund or credit or wait until new Notice of Allowance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection after allowance and requirement for primary examiner approval
rubrics_metrics.description: A claim noted as allowable shall thereafter be rejected only with the approval of the primary examiner; great care should be exercised in authorizing such rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a new reference is discovered that is obviously applicable to allowed claims, a memorandum should be addressed to the TC Director citing the reference and briefly stating its application; submit the memorandum with the reference and file wrapper (if in paper). If the request to withdraw from issue is approved, the TC Director withdraws the application and the examiner prepares an Office action rejecting the claims in view of the reference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality Review Program for examined patent applications
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office of Patent Quality Assurance administers a program that randomly samples allowed applications from each examiner to review the quality of examination and increase likelihood of validity of issued patents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review Quality Assurance Specialists independently review sampled allowed applications (some subsamples are also independently searched). Excluded from sampling are applications with Board or court decisions. If reviewers determine one or more claims are unpatentable, the application will be reopened; use form paragraph 13.04 (Reopen Prosecution) and, if issue fee was paid, include form paragraph 13.05 (Vacate Notice of Allowance). Quality Assurance forms/papers must not be included in Office actions or retained in the file; the record should not indicate a review occurred.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraphs for reopening prosecution after Notice of Allowance
rubrics_metrics.description: When prosecution is reopened after the Notice of Allowance because claim(s) are considered unpatentable, use form paragraph 13.04 (Reopen Prosecution - After Notice of Allowance) and, where applicable, form paragraph 13.05 (Reopen Prosecution - Vacate Notice of Allowance).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ¶13.04 states the claim(s) considered unpatentable and the reasons; ¶13.05 advises applicant that the prior Notice of Allowance is vacated and explains refund/credit treatment of issue/publication fees if already paid. ¶13.04 must be used when rejecting previously allowed claim(s); ¶13.05 must be used when prosecution is reopened after mailing of the Notice of Allowance and the issue fee has been paid.
